- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes or negative sentiment — adjust downward bias by 2–5% of recent range.
- Lagged forecasts tend to overreact to recent sentiment shifts — smooth out 3–5 day moving averages before final adjustment.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly bearish (0.0–0.4), model often overcorrects — reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior period.
- Avoid over-optimistic forecasts when sentiment is volatile — cap forecast growth to 1.5x recent average unless sentiment > 0.7.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast exceeds 20% above recent 10-day high, reduce by 10–15% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overshoot early in trend — cap final 5–7 days to 10% below peak if sentiment is fading.
